name: Fernpass
kurzbeschreibung: The 1,216 m high Fernpass connects Reutte with Nassereith, featuring historic mountain routes, landslide forests, and turquoise lakes.
dauer: Driving time approx. 30 minutes; as an excursion with hiking 2 to 4 hours
oeffnungszeiten: Open year-round (winter tires and snow chains mandatory in snow conditions)
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Fernpass links the Tyrolean Zugspitz Arena with the Upper Inn Valley at an altitude of 1,216 meters and ranks among Austria's busiest and most picturesque alpine crossings. Nestled between the towering Mieming Range to the east and the Lechtal Alps to the west, today's mountain pass landscape was shaped roughly 4,000 years ago by an enormous prehistoric rockslide. The cascading rock debris created an enchanted topography of forested knolls, gigantic boulders, and crystalline mountain lakes including the emerald-green Blindsee, idyllic Mittersee, and romantic Fernsteinsee. The Romans developed the crossing into the military road Via Claudia Augusta. Today, travelers experience an inspiring fusion of historical transportation legacy, high-alpine panoramas, and diverse outdoor recreation in the heart of the Tyrolean Alps.

Route & Requirements

The B179 Fernpassstraße is a modern, well-maintained federal road with gentle gradients (maximum 8 percent) that is toll-free and passable year-round. It is fully suitable for passenger cars, motorcycles, and coaches; heavy freight traffic is subject to strict weight restrictions. For hikers and mountain bikers, the Fernpass provides excellent terrain: the historic Via Claudia Augusta route runs away from road traffic, offering gravel cyclists and leisure hikers a tranquil nature experience. A popular walk leads from the pass crest down to pristine Lake Blindsee (approx. 1 hour). Sturdy hiking boots and standard fitness are recommended away from paved surfaces. Scuba divers revere Lake Blindsee for its underwater visibility through submerged tree trunks.

Visit & Arrival

The Fernpass is open year-round around the clock as a vital transit link; mandatory winter equipment regulations apply during snowfall. Numerous viewing bays and roadside rest areas allow scenic pauses with sweeping views across the peaks. Drivers from Germany travel toll-free via the A7 via Füssen and Reutte, or from the Inntal through Nassereith. Public VVT regional bus route 150 connects the railway stations of Imst-Pitztal and Reutte in Tirol on a regular schedule, stopping directly at the pass summit.

Tips

Make sure to pull over at the scenic overlook above Lake Blindsee – the view of the turquoise waters framed by the Zugspitze massif is an iconic photo motif. Stop by historic Schloss Fernsteinsee on the southern pass approach for coffee and Tyrolean pastries in a grand setting.
